SECTION II Curricular Matters Which Require Confirmation by the Faculty Senate NEW PROGRAMS: COLLEGE OF EDUCATION AND PROFESSIONAL STUDIES: School of Education: BA in World Language Education (All grades): The School of Education currently offers a Bachelor of Arts degree in Secondary Education, with multiple tracks reflecting various specializations.
Since its inception, the World Language Education Program has been one of these tracks (the other tracks are English, History/Social Studies, Mathematics, and Science).
Upon graduation, students in the Secondary Education Program obtain certification to teach at the High School level (grades 7-12).

Upon the completion of an additional course and a teaching practicum at a Middle School, students in this existing program also have the option to obtain a Middle School extension, a credential that allows them to teach in grades 5-8 in any Rhode Island elementary, middle, or junior high school.
Recently the Rhode Island Department of Education changed the World Language teacher certification system.
Due to these changes, graduates from our current Secondary Education – World Language program are now certified to teach in Rhode Island at all levels of elementary, middle, and secondary education (grades PK-12).
The new program proposal is intended to address the changes in Rhode Island certification regulations, which will require significant changes (over 25%) to the requirements for our current BA in Secondary Education with a specialization in World Languages, effectively transforming it into a BA in World Language Education-All Grades.

In the proposed new program, students will take a variety of existing EDC courses in Elementary Education, Early Childhood Education, Secondary Education, and Teaching English as a Second Language / Bilingual Education concentrations so that, upon graduation, they will be more versatile and highly employable educators who are better prepared to teach effectively in a wider variety of educational settings.
The new program will educate our students to become reflective teachers committed to global citizenship, social justice, and multicultural education.
Our program of study, based on current research and best practices, has been carefully crafted to provide our teacher candidates with ample opportunities to learn about different professional contexts and acquire knowledge about learning theory (social, emotional, and academic), and how to address the individualized needs of diverse learners.
Through a 1

variety of hands-on teaching experiences at PK-12 academic settings our candidates will have the opportunity to apply what they learn in URI courses in culturally responsive practices but also to learn to work with and from practicing teachers. The standard program of study that our candidates will follow will allow them to graduate from URI with a double major in Education and in a Foreign Language. Students will develop their teaching skills and acquire knowledge through coursework that focuses on teaching and learning at different developmental levels, and on cutting-edge second language acquisition theories. Our program will help teacher candidates develop the necessary confidence and experience to effectively engage with a diverse group of students in a variety of educational settings. Upon completion of our program and after successfully completing the licensure tests, our well prepared graduates will be ready to apply for the Rhode Island World Language teacher certification in grades K-12. 2

The RIDE certification requirements for World Language teachers are:4 ● Bachelor’s degree from a regionally accredited institution ● Completion of an approved program or Credential Review Consortium Institution (CRCI) credential review plan for the preparation of All Grades World Language Teachers in a specific language ● Completion of a minimum of 12 weeks of student teaching in this area and a minimum of 60 hours field experience prior to student teaching ● Demonstration of meeting the pedagogical competencies of the Rhode Island Professional Teaching Standards (RIPTS) ● Demonstration of meeting the content competencies as prescribed by the American Council for the Teaching of Foreign Languages (ACTFL) Other requirements: ● Meet all Rhode Island pedagogy and subject matter testing requirements for this certificate area 4 See: <https://www.ride.ri.gov/Portals/0/Uploads/Documents/Teachers-and-Administrators-Excellent- Educators/Educator-Certification/Cert-Requirements/tbd_AG-World%20Languages-Req.pdf?ver=2015-01-22- 123036-823>.

In addition to this, the RI Department of Education, through the work of the Rhode Island Council on Elementary and Secondary Education, is currently in the process of changing the state’s high school graduation requirements.
